meta.source: Luminari AZ Three-Layer Registry v1.0 — Northwest Hope Foundation

steps.action: Document the violation with timestamps. Photograph the issue. Keep all correspondence with landlord in writing. Note dates, times, conditions. AZ Residential Landlord and Tenant Act (ARS §33-1324) requires landlord to maintain habitable premises.
steps.documents_needed: Photos, written communications, lease copy
steps.notes: Creates paper trail. AZ ARLTA applies to most residential rentals. CRITICAL: Heat/AC is a habitability issue in AZ — landlord must maintain cooling systems.

steps.action: Send written notice to landlord stating the violation, citing ARS §33-1361. Give landlord 10 BUSINESS DAYS to remedy for non-emergency repairs. For emergency conditions (no AC in summer, no water), landlord must act within 5 days or tenant may exercise remedies.
steps.documents_needed: Written notice to landlord (certified mail recommended)
steps.deadline: Immediately after documenting — creates paper trail
steps.statute: ARS §33-1361 (Noncompliance by Landlord), ARS §33-1365 (Damage or Destruction)
steps.notes: 10-business-day repair deadline is AZ-specific. For heat emergencies, shorter timeline applies. Tenant may repair and deduct up to $300 or half month's rent (whichever is greater) after proper notice.

steps.action: File complaint with local code enforcement. Phoenix: Neighborhood Services (602-262-7456). Tucson: Code Enforcement (520-791-5843). Other cities: contact city/county code enforcement. For heat emergencies, also contact AZ Heat Relief Network (211).
steps.documents_needed: Photos, correspondence, lease
steps.state_agency: Phoenix Neighborhood Services / Tucson Code Enforcement
steps.notes: Code enforcement is local in AZ. Phoenix and Tucson have strongest enforcement. For heat emergencies (no AC in summer), this is a LIFE SAFETY issue — call 211 for cooling stations.

steps.action: Contact legal aid for tenant representation. CLS AZ (Phoenix/Maricopa) or SALA (Tucson/Southern AZ). For tribal housing issues, contact DNA People's Legal Services.
steps.documents_needed: All documentation, lease, correspondence, code enforcement reports
steps.state_agency: CLS AZ / SALA / DNA People's Legal
steps.deadline: Before any court hearing — immediately if eviction filed
steps.statute: ARS §33-1381 (Retaliatory Conduct), ARS §33-1375 (Wrongful Failure to Supply Essential Services)
steps.notes: AZ has anti-retaliation protections. Landlord cannot retaliate for code complaints. For tribal land housing, tribal courts may have jurisdiction.

steps.action: File complaint with AZ Attorney General Consumer Protection or HUD Fair Housing. AG handles consumer fraud and pattern violations. HUD handles discrimination complaints.
steps.documents_needed: All documentation including code enforcement results
steps.state_agency: AZ Attorney General / HUD Region IX
steps.deadline: HUD: within 1 year of violation. AG: no strict deadline
steps.statute: ARS §44-1521 (Consumer Fraud Act), Fair Housing Act 42 USC §3601
steps.notes: HUD complaint triggers federal investigation. AZ AG can pursue pattern cases. AZ Civil Rights Division handles state discrimination claims.

steps.action: File lawsuit in AZ Justice Court (claims < $3,500) or Superior Court. Tenant may seek damages, injunctive relief, attorney fees under ARS §33-1381.
steps.documents_needed: All documentation, legal aid referral, filing fee (waiver available)
steps.state_agency: AZ Justice Court / AZ Superior Court
steps.deadline: Statute of limitations: 1 year for lease violations, 2 years for property damage
steps.notes: AZ allows attorney fee recovery for prevailing tenant under ARLTA. Justice Court is faster and cheaper for smaller claims.

steps.action: Document all unpaid wages. Keep records of hours worked, pay stubs, employment agreements, text messages about work. AZ minimum wage is $14.70/hr (Jan 2026). Flagstaff has higher local minimum wage.
steps.documents_needed: Pay stubs, time records, employment agreement, text/email communications
steps.deadline: Immediately — 1-YEAR statute of limitations for wage claims (shorter than most states!)
steps.notes: CRITICAL: AZ has only a 1-YEAR SOL for wage claims — much shorter than federal 2-year FLSA SOL. Document immediately. Flagstaff minimum wage is higher than state minimum.

steps.action: File wage claim with AZ Industrial Commission (ICA). ICA handles minimum wage, overtime, and final paycheck violations. Employer must pay final wages within 7 days of termination or next regular payday (whichever is sooner).
steps.documents_needed: Completed ICA wage claim form, pay stubs, employment records
steps.notes: 1-YEAR SOL is critical — do not delay. ICA investigates and can order payment. Employer owes treble damages for willful violations. Final paycheck must be paid within 7 days.

steps.action: File complaint with AZ Civil Rights Division (CRD) if wage theft involves discrimination. File with EEOC if federal discrimination applies.
steps.documents_needed: Wage claim documentation, evidence of discrimination
steps.deadline: CRD: 180 days. EEOC: 300 days (with CRD cross-filing)
steps.statute: ARS §41-1463 (AZ Civil Rights Act), Title VII
steps.notes: CRD and EEOC have worksharing agreement. Filing with one preserves rights with other.

steps.action: Contact legal aid for representation. CLS AZ (Phoenix/Maricopa) or SALA (Tucson/Southern AZ). For federal wage claims, contact DOL Wage and Hour Division.
steps.documents_needed: All documentation, ICA claim results
steps.deadline: Federal FLSA: 2 years (3 years if willful)
steps.notes: Federal FLSA has longer SOL (2-3 years) than AZ state claim (1 year). Consider filing both. DOL can investigate federal minimum wage and overtime violations.

steps.action: File lawsuit in AZ court. Justice Court for claims < $3,500, Superior Court for larger claims. Prevailing employee may recover treble damages and attorney fees.
steps.documents_needed: All documentation, legal representation
steps.state_agency: AZ Justice Court / AZ Superior Court
steps.deadline: Within 1 year of violation (state) or 2-3 years (federal FLSA)
steps.notes: AZ allows treble damages for willful wage violations. Class/collective actions possible under FLSA.

steps.action: Request written denial notice. All benefit programs must provide written notice of denial, reduction, or termination with appeal rights. Keep the denial letter — it contains your appeal deadline.
steps.documents_needed: Denial letter, application materials, supporting documents
steps.notes: CRITICAL: AZ has very short appeal deadlines. UI appeal: 15 DAYS. SNAP: 30 days. AHCCCS: 90 days. Read denial letter carefully for your specific deadline.

steps.action: File appeal within deadline. SNAP: 30 days for fair hearing. AHCCCS: 60 days for grievance, 90 days for appeal. UI: 15 DAYS (very short!). TANF: 30 days. Request continued benefits pending appeal if currently receiving.
steps.documents_needed: Denial letter, appeal form, supporting evidence
steps.deadline: UI: 15 DAYS. SNAP: 30 days. TANF: 30 days. AHCCCS: 90 days.
steps.notes: UI 15-day deadline is one of the shortest in the US. Mark calendar immediately. Request aid-paid-pending for SNAP/AHCCCS if filing within 10 days of denial.

steps.action: Contact legal aid for representation at hearing. CLS AZ (Phoenix), SALA (Tucson), or ACDL (disability-related denials). For AHCCCS managed care denials, also contact the managed care plan's grievance department.
steps.documents_needed: All documentation, denial letter, appeal filing confirmation
steps.notes: Legal representation significantly improves hearing outcomes. ACDL specializes in disability benefit denials.

steps.action: Attend fair hearing. DES hearings are by phone or in person. Bring all documentation. You may have a representative. The hearing officer's decision is binding unless appealed to Superior Court.
steps.documents_needed: All evidence, witness list, legal representative
steps.notes: Missing the hearing results in dismissal. Request continuance if needed. Phone hearings are common in AZ.

steps.action: If denied at hearing, appeal to AZ Superior Court (judicial review). File within 35 days of final administrative decision. Contact legal aid for court representation.
steps.documents_needed: Hearing decision, all prior documentation, legal representation
steps.notes: Judicial review is on the administrative record — no new evidence. Court reviews for abuse of discretion.

steps.action: File federal complaint if systemic issues. Contact HHS Office for Civil Rights for Medicaid access issues. Contact USDA for SNAP systemic issues. Contact DOL for UI systemic issues.
steps.documents_needed: All documentation, evidence of systemic pattern
steps.notes: Federal complaints appropriate when state system has systemic failures or discrimination patterns.

steps.action: Request written denial with specific reason codes. Review your policy for covered benefits. Document all communications with insurer. Keep copies of all claims and EOBs.
steps.documents_needed: Denial letter, EOB, policy/certificate of coverage, claim forms
steps.notes: AZ has strong external review rights under ARS §20-2533. For AHCCCS managed care, separate grievance process applies.

steps.action: File internal appeal with insurance company. Most plans allow 180 days for internal appeal. Request expedited review for urgent medical situations. For AHCCCS managed care, file grievance with the plan.
steps.documents_needed: Appeal letter, supporting medical records, doctor's letter of medical necessity
steps.notes: Internal appeal is usually required before external review. Expedited review available for urgent situations.

steps.action: File complaint with AZ Department of Insurance and Financial Institutions (DIFI). DIFI regulates all insurance in AZ and investigates consumer complaints.
steps.documents_needed: Denial letter, appeal results, all correspondence
steps.notes: DIFI investigates and can take enforcement action against insurers. Also handles agent/broker complaints.

steps.action: Request external review through DIFI. AZ provides independent external review for health insurance denials. For AHCCCS, request AHCCCS fair hearing.
steps.documents_needed: Internal appeal denial, all medical records, external review request form
steps.notes: External review is binding on the insurer. Independent medical experts review the denial. AHCCCS has separate administrative hearing process.

steps.action: Contact legal aid or file lawsuit. CLS AZ or SALA for low-income individuals. Private attorneys for bad faith claims. AZ allows bad faith lawsuits against insurers.
steps.documents_needed: All documentation, external review results
steps.deadline: Varies by claim type — typically 2 years for bad faith
steps.statute: ARS §20-1110, Rawlings v. Apodaca (AZ bad faith standard)
steps.notes: AZ recognizes insurance bad faith as a tort. Punitive damages available for egregious conduct. ERISA preempts state claims for employer-sponsored plans.

steps.action: File federal complaint if applicable. CMS for Medicare/Medicaid issues. DOL for ERISA plan violations. CFPB for financial product insurance.
steps.documents_needed: All documentation, evidence of federal law violation
steps.notes: Federal remedies supplement state remedies. CMS handles Medicare Advantage and Part D denials.
